topic: Cursor 3.1 Review 2026: Tiled Layout, Multi-Model Comparison, and Cloud Agent Environments

competitors.title: Meet the new Cursor (Cursor 3 Launch)
key_points: Cursor 3 is a unified workspace for building software with agents, launched April 2, 2026
New interface built from scratch centered around agents, not files
Multi-workspace layout allowing humans and agents to work across different repos simultaneously
All local and cloud agents appear in sidebar including those from mobile, web, Slack, GitHub, and Linear
Seamless handoff between local and cloud agents — move sessions between environments
Composer 2 (own frontier coding model) integrated for fast iteration
New diffs view for editing and reviewing changes with simpler UI
Integrated browser for agents to navigate and test local websites
Cursor Marketplace with hundreds of plugins (MCPs, skills, subagents)

competitors.title: Introducing Composer 2
key_points: Composer 2 launched March 19, 2026 — frontier-level coding model
Priced at $0.50/M input and $2.50/M output tokens
CursorBench: 61.3, Terminal-Bench 2.0: 61.7, SWE-bench Multilingual: 73.7
First continued pretraining run providing stronger base for RL scaling
Fast variant at $1.50/M input and $7.50/M output tokens with same intelligence
Composer 2.5 now powers Bugbot (June 2026)

competitors.title: Development environments for your cloud agents
key_points: Cloud agents need full development environments to close the loop on work
Multi-repo environments support — agents can work across multiple codebases
Dockerfile-based configuration as code with build secrets support
Layer caching: 70% faster rebuilds on cache hits
Agent-led environment setup with validation and questions
Environment governance: version history, rollback, audit logs
Egress and secrets scoped at development environment level
Environment configuration committed to .cursor/environment.json

competitors.title: What we've learned building cloud agents
key_points: Cloud agents run on dedicated VMs with own environments, dependencies, and network access
Development environment is the single biggest factor in output quality
Migrated to Temporal for durable execution — survives inference outages, pod failures
Temporal handles 50M+ actions/day across 7M+ unique workflows
40%+ of Cursor's own PRs come from cloud agents
Decoupled agent loop, machine state, and conversation state
Self-healing agent environments with autoinstall capability
Cloud agents need different prompts than local — more autonomous, less blocking

angles: Cursor 3.1 represents the shift from file-centric to agent-centric development — the IDE becomes a command center for AI agents
Tiled layout and multi-workspace support enable developers to run multiple agents across repos simultaneously, fundamentally changing the development workflow
Multi-model comparison (judge feature) lets developers run the same prompt across multiple models and pick the best result — a new paradigm for AI-assisted coding
Cloud agent environments solve the 'works on my machine' problem for AI agents, with Dockerfile-as-code, environment governance, and self-healing capabilities
Cursor's rapid ARR growth ($500M → $1B → $2B in ~9 months) signals enterprise AI coding adoption is accelerating faster than any previous developer tool category
The Composer 2 model family (2, 2.5) shows Cursor is investing in proprietary models optimized for agentic coding, not just wrapping third-party APIs
Cursor Automations and cloud agents are turning the IDE into a 24/7 development platform — agents that respond to Slack, GitHub events, and run unattended
The pricing backlash ($20 Pro → $40-50 actual spend) and tightening usage limits create tension between individual developers and enterprise adoption
